summary: Task 9 (auth pages translation) introduces no new security regressions. Information disclosure surface is closed: useApiError only reads the numeric HTTP status from the error object and resolves the user-visible string via a te()-gated locale chain (errors.<ctx>.<status> -> errors.<ctx>.generic -> errors.generic -> empty), falling back to an empty string when no key matches. None of the five page-level catch blocks bypass the factory or concatenate raw error fields (e.message / e.data / e.response._data) into submitError. forgot-password.vue preserves the silent-catch / always-true `submitted.value = true` contract (email-enumeration protection retained); useApiError is intentionally not injected there. The ?token= query parameter on reset-password.vue and verify-email.vue is consumed only for (a) routing/state branching via boolean coercion (!token.value, no-token state) and (b) the outbound request to the backend (request body in reset-password, query param in verify-email). The token is never rendered in the template, never logged, never injected into useHead/useSeoMeta/canonical/hreflang (those APIs are not used on auth pages or in their layouts), and the route-rule headers from Task 2/3 (Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, X-Robots-Tag: noindex,nofollow on both /auth/** and /<locale>/auth/**) remain unchanged. Zod schema correctness is preserved across all five pages: register and reset-password retain min(8) + letter refine + digit refine + outer passwords-match refine; the entire chain is rebuilt by the computed when locale.value changes, so locale switches regenerate messages without weakening constraints. The VITEST conditional in nuxt.config.ts uses process.env.VITEST, which Vitest itself populates for the test runner and is not set by Node/Vite/Nuxt dev/build/production runtimes — locale detection in production is unaffected. No hardcoded secrets, no XSS surface (no v-html, only t() output and form errors), no SSRF (client-side), and no logging or deserialization risks introduced.

non_blocking_findings.title: Empty catch in useApiError fallback returns empty string instead of generic error key
non_blocking_findings.description:
useApiError() in frontend/composables/useApiError.ts:34 returns an empty string when no candidate key resolves through te(). In practice the chain ends with `errors.generic`, which Task 4 should populate, so this branch is unreachable in normal operation. Still, an empty submitError causes the

block to render nothing, which silently swallows an unexpected error condition (eg. a missing locale dictionary) without surfacing anything to the user or the console. This is not a vulnerability per se, but it reduces observability of an i18n-config regression and could mask a security-relevant error path during incident response. Consider returning a hardcoded last-resort English string and/or emitting a console.warn when te() rejects every candidate, so a missing-key regression is visible.
non_blocking_findings.impact: Reduced observability of locale-dictionary regressions; not exploitable, but could obscure error paths during debugging/incident response.
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Return a hardcoded fallback (eg. 'Something went wrong') from the final return and log a console.warn(`[useApiError] no locale key resolved for ${candidates.join(', ')}`) when the loop exits without a hit. This guarantees the user always sees a non-empty message and the warning makes a missing-key regression visible in dev/test.

non_blocking_findings.title: Token query parameter persists in browser address bar and history
non_blocking_findings.description: On /auth/reset-password?token=... and /auth/verify-email?token=..., the token remains in the address bar and browser history for the duration the page is open. Route-level Referrer-Policy: no-referrer (set in nuxt.config.ts via Task 2/3) and X-Robots-Tag: noindex,nofollow already mitigate the principal cross-site / crawler leakage vectors. However, the token is still visible to: (a) browser-history sync to other devices via signed-in browsers (Chrome Sync, Firefox Sync), (b) shoulder-surfing or screenshot/screen-share, (c) browser extensions that read the URL, (d) clipboard copy if the user copies the URL. This is a property of the email-link design (not introduced by Task 9) and the backend tokens are presumably single-use and short-lived, but Task 9 is the natural place to document the residual risk. As an optional hardening, consider stripping the query parameter from the URL after the page reads it on mount (using history.replaceState or router.replace) so the token disappears from the address bar and any subsequent in-page navigation history entry. verify-email.vue already moves to a state (success/expired/invalid) that doesn't depend on the token after the initial verify() call; reset-password.vue keeps a reactive dependency on token until submit, but the token could be captured into a local non-reactive variable on mount and then stripped from route.query.
non_blocking_findings.impact: Token visible in URL bar / browser history during page session; mitigated by short-lived single-use backend tokens and Referrer-Policy/X-Robots-Tag headers, but visible to local-device exfiltration vectors (history sync, screenshots, extensions).
non_blocking_findings.recommendation: Optional: on mount, after capturing the token into a local non-reactive variable, call `await router.replace({ query: {} })` or `history.replaceState({}, '', location.pathname)` to remove the token from the address bar. This keeps the token out of subsequent history entries and out of any URL the user might copy. Verify Vitest specs still pass (route.query.token captured before replace) before shipping. Out of scope for Task 9 acceptance criteria — flag for follow-up.
